public_rationale: The contemporary public research record supports the ordinary reading. OpenAI called reliable refusal of unsafe instructions an open problem. Sparrow's additional safety and grounding methods still produced failures, and Galactica explicitly lacked truthfulness guarantees. These records distinguish substantial mitigation from the complete protection Marcus specified. They do not establish that such protection is impossible forever.
limitations: This is a historical assessment of established methods, not a mathematical impossibility theorem.
The cited systems do not exhaust every possible model or private experiment.
Substantial safety improvements are compatible with the claim's 100% threshold.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs are unruly, and nobody knows how to make them refrain 100% of the time from insulting users, giving bad advice, or making stuff up.

statement.excerpt: LLMs are unruly beasts; nobody knows how to make them refrain 100% of time from insulting users, giving bad advice, or just plain making stuff up.
statement.document_title: How come smart assistants have virtually no ability to converse, despite all the spectacular progress with large language models?

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading concerns useful, open-ended language systems and the publicly established methods available when the post appeared.
A system that remains silent or returns only fixed approved text is outside the conversational capability discussed in the post.
The claim concerns complete protection, not whether researchers could substantially reduce harmful or false outputs.

For this ongoing research-state observation, I use the current year's public research record through the post: 2022-01-01 to 2022-11-22. This is an evaluator-selected reporting window, not a date range supplied by Marcus.
Support means the documented research state treated complete protection as unsolved; it does not require proving what every person privately knew.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary accounts of leading protection methods document remaining harmful or fabricated outputs and treat reliable prevention as an open problem, with no established method providing all three protections universally.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A method known by the post date demonstrably guaranteed all three protections across the intended open-ended use of a useful LLM.

evidence.explanation: OpenAI described reliable refusal of unsafe instructions as unsolved despite improvements from human-feedback training. Its limitations section also reports remaining toxic outputs and fabricated facts.

Sparrow combined human feedback, explicit behavioral rules, and supporting evidence. The paper still reports incomplete factual support and rule violations under adversarial probing; these improvements did not provide universal protection.
